translations.english: Refactor src/net/client.py so that its retry logic uses a backoff that doubles its wait time after every attempt. Limit the attempts to 5. Do not change the public interface.
Turn the user's question into a SQL query against the sales database, run it, and write out only the results — do not write out the query.
I have handled 1,200 records out of 3,000 so far. The job will probably finish in about 25 minutes, based on the current rate.
Every unit test passes on my machine. I am waiting for the tests that exercise the whole system; I will open a merge request after they finish.
This search found 14 results. The most relevant one is the official changelog at https://docs.python.org/3/whatsnew/3.13.html, which lists the removed modules.
The calculation confirms that the budget covers the total cost, but the remaining budget is small.
Should the summary target executives, or should it target the [edition]? The level of technical detail depends on the audience.
About last quarter: do you mean the most recent ordinary calendar quarter, or do you mean the company's fiscal quarter?
The payment API request failed with HTTP 503 on three consecutive attempts. I stopped retrying, so I will not hit the maximum rate limit.
The step that translates the document failed, because the input is larger than the maximum context size. I can split the document into pieces and retry. Should I do that?

I propose three steps. Let's collect the customer complaint reports, then group them by theme, then order the themes by their count. The second step is the hardest, so I want a second reviewer on it. I will start the collection if you do not [object]. Expect the first results within the next hour.
We can add a cache in front of the slow query, and then we do not have to rewrite the whole module again. That is lower [risk — literally 'lower ten'], and rolling it back is easy.
The patch is correct, but the loop in merge_records() reads every row for every row. It will be too slow with 100,000 rows, so you should consider a hash table keyed by ID.
The summary is good overall. It is slightly too long. It will not be longer than the limit if you cut the background section.
I agree with your plan, with one change: run the cheaper model first, and use the larger one only for the hard cases.
I do not agree with the plan that drops the outliers: they are real measurements [agr — unclear, perhaps 'incoming'], and a fault causes them. So we should flag them, and we should not delete them.
Australia's capital is Canberra; it is not Sydney. My confidence is high. The sources are the Australian government website and two reference books.

That is correct. The bug was fixed in version 4.2.1. The changelog at https://github.com/example-org/tilemap/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md confirms that. I tested the fix on my machine. My confidence is high.

This is a handoff. My fix is on the branch fix/login-timeout. I have not yet updated test_auth.py; that is the rest of the work. The unreliable test is test_session_expiry, which fails in roughly 1 run out of 10.

This is the state of things so far. The Lisbon flight is booked for the two people travelling, but the hotel is not booked yet. The user wants to stay near the old town. The rest of the budget is 850 EUR.
